mechanism.question: Can !!js be used as a SEQUENCE ELEMENT (an entry inside toolFilter.allow), not just as a scalar row field? vendor/include's own doc comment only promises '!!js SCALARS'.
loaderSource: vendor/include/src/index.ts:9 — const JsExpr = new yaml.Type('tag:yaml.org,2002:js', { kind: 'scalar', construct: (data) => ({ __jsExpr: data }) }). A tagged scalar inside a sequence is still a scalar node, so the tag applies.

cordis-plugin-loader/lib/index.js — function interpolate(ctx, value) { if (isJsExpr(value)) return evaluate(ctx, value.__jsExpr); ... else if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.map((item) => interpolate(ctx, item)); ... } — array elements are interpolated explicitly.
mechanism.precedent: Shipped preset packages/preset/agent-presets/presets/cordis/agent.cordis.yml:260 already uses a tagged !!js node as a list element; the user's dsh-programming-mode preset does the same.

quotingTrap.unquotedResult: PARSES AS VALID YAML BUT NOT AS AN EXPRESSION NODE — it becomes a COMPLEX MAPPING KEY. Measured with the loader's own js-yaml schema: allow = ['read', {'[object Object]':'bash'}, 'lsp']. Silent, and it produces a NON-STRING allow entry.
quotingTrap.quotedResult: allow = ['read', 'bash', 'lsp'] on darwin — a proper string. This is the form shipped, matching presets/cordis/agent.cordis.yml:260.
quotingTrap.whyItMatters: The unquoted form fails SILENTLY at the YAML layer and would surface only as an obscure allow-list type error later — the exact class of invisible failure this project's 'fail visible' constraint exists to prevent.

findingThisRound.claim: The verifier enumerated role names INSIDE its role-detection regex — a third hand-maintained registry besides the yml allow-lists and EXPECTED, with no comment marking it.
findingThisRound.evidence: scripts/verify-agent-lanes.cjs:156 previously matched a regex whose alternation literally listed (explorer|librarian|oracle|fixer). Adding EXPECTED.designer alone would NOT have been enough: a designer session would have fallen into the no-role branch and printed the persona-injection WARN, so EXPECTED.designer would never have been consulted.
findingThisRound.whyItMatters: Silent misdiagnosis: that WARN blames persona injection rather than the missing registry entry, and it is emitted in the same bucket as genuinely unregistered new roles.
findingThisRound.fix: Replaced the alternation with a generic lowercase-role capture; registration is now decided solely by EXPECTED, and an unregistered role gets the explicit new-role WARN.
findingThisRound.verified: The new regex discriminates correctly on four cases: designer -> designer, explorer -> explorer, a brandnew unregistered role -> brandnew (then the EXPECTED WARN), and the orchestrator lane-table text -> undefined (the You-are anchor still prevents false matches).

howToReproduce: Mechanism test (zero cost): parse the real composition with the loader dialect and interpolate it — the source lines to copy are vendor/include/src/index.ts:9 (the js-yaml Type) and cordis-plugin-loader/lib/index.js (interpolate).

Host mount (requires a NEW session): confirm designer appears in the orchestrator's delegation tool surface, delegate one designer, then run node scripts/verify-agent-lanes.cjs — the designer row must read role=designer ptc=no with the whitelist exact match (6 items + the two known self-layer leaks).
